correctness.rationale: For K=H−iγΠ, the imaginary part of any eigenvalue is −γ||Πu||²/||u||². The dark space is the direct sum over E of ker(H−E) intersected with ker Π (not merely the sum of full eigenspaces contained in ker Π). It reduces H and Π. The complement has strictly negative imaginary spectrum, so it decays even with Jordan blocks. The survival limit is the squared dark-projection norm; trace over untrapped sites gives ν/(N−2). Independent derivation of the count: gauge all bonds real except the seam at 0. A dark eigenvector has to solve the Dirichlet problem on both arcs of edge lengths d and N−d. A nonzero wave on only one arc cannot cancel at the first sink because its first neighbor's sine amplitude is nonzero. A common phase is q=πa/h, 1≤a<h, h=gcd(N,d). With m=ad/h and n=a(N−d)/h, matching at d fixes the ratio of arc amplitudes to (−1)^m and matching at 0 requires exp(iφ)=(−1)^(m+n)=(−1)^(aN/h). There is one dimension per allowed a, and none if either arc has length 1. This yields all three cases of the quoted count and trichotomy, including odd N and adjacent traps. For fixed total flux, redistributing bond phases is itself unitarily gauge-equivalent and cannot change the count or sitewise survival; the caution about such redistribution in the frozen Limitations is misleading, but not a flaw in the Finding under its stated assumptions.
residual_risks: The source's 5,473 numerical assertions are recorded finite evidence, not an independent replay or proof for all N. The theorem concerns the continuous dissipative generator, not arbitrary timed projective monitoring.
